findings.title: ConfigEntryNotReady from the first refresh leaks the coordinator's listeners and MQTT subscription per retry
findings.claim: When the first refresh raises ConfigEntryNotReady (Tibber unreachable at boot), the coordinator built by that setup keeps its async_track_state_change_event registrations and ECL110 MQTT subscription forever, and each setup retry leaks another coordinator.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.__init__ spawns _async_setup_peak_guard, _async_setup_defrost_watch and _async_setup_ecl110_state_subscription before async_setup_entry awaits async_config_entry_first_refresh; they register directly on hass, not via entry.async_on_unload. On ConfigEntryNotReady Home Assistant runs only entry.async_on_unload callbacks and cancels entry background tasks; async_unload_entry / coordinator.async_shutdown never run. The bound methods on the bus keep the dead coordinator alive and its _on_power_event runs on every meter event. The ECL110 state topic defaults on, so MQTT installs leak the subscription even with both guards off.

Real HA: configure the peak guard with a power meter (or a defrost entity, or MQTT with the default ECL110 state topic), make api.tibber.com unreachable, restart HA, wait through several setup retries, restore the network; every retry left a coordinator subscribed.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: One place: in async_setup_entry catch ConfigEntryNotReady from the first refresh and call coordinator.async_shutdown() before re-raising; or move the three registrations after the first refresh / behind entry.async_on_unload.

findings.title: Reload during a scheduled solve: the torn-down coordinator actuates the pump and writes stores after its own shutdown
findings.claim: An options reload while the scheduled refresh is inside the executor lets the old coordinator finish _async_update_data after async_shutdown returned: it commands the switch, publishes two MQTT commands from the pre-reload plan and writes two stores, concurrently with the new instance's setup.
findings.mechanism: async_shutdown's docstring says the base class stops any in-flight refresh; Home Assistant's DataUpdateCoordinator.async_shutdown cancels only the scheduled timer and the debouncer, and a scheduled refresh is a hass-level task that entry unload does not cancel (only entry background tasks are, which is why the first solve is clean). Nothing after the executor await in async_run_optimization or before _apply_action in _async_update_data checks _shutdown_requested.

findings.title: Store loaders crash on corrupt payloads; three stores are never reset so the loss repeats on every restart
findings.claim: 152 of 2000 seeded corrupt payloads (200 per store, 10 stores) end the store's fire-and-forget loader with an unhandled exception; for dhw_profile (64/200), thermal_learning (9/200) and dhw_draws (1/200) the corrupt file is never rewritten, so every restart raises again and the learned state stays lost, with thermal_learning left half-applied.
findings.mechanism: Each loader guards only store.async_load(); the parsing after it trusts the shape. _normalize_dhw_profile np.clips whatever the 24-element list holds; _async_load_thermal_learning catches (TypeError, ValueError) but int(inf) raises OverflowError, a wrapped freq_map raises KeyError, a top-level list raises AttributeError on .get; PriceShapeModel.from_dict float()s shapes/quarter_factors unguarded; DefrostDerate/StartCounter/AccuracyTracker.from_dict hit the same OverflowError/KeyError paths. accuracy, energy_totals, ledger, price_model are rewritten by the next cycle or learned day (repeat 0, history lost); the three above are written only on learning events. The update loop never fails (cycle1_failed=0, cycle2_failed=0 in 2000/2000).

findings.title: A price list no longer covering the horizon is planned and actuated on a flat 0.5 price while the cycle stays green
findings.claim: When _prices is non-empty but no entry covers any step of the horizon, every step is priced at extend_price_series' fallback constant 0.5, the solve runs, publishes savings_percentage and predicted_cost, actuates the switch, and _async_update_data succeeds.
findings.mechanism: _price_series returns None (skip the run) only when self._prices is empty; _known_prices_for yields an empty leading run for a stale list and price_model.extend_price_series returns np.full(n_steps, fallback=0.5) with known_count == 0 — the invented flat curve the _price_series docstring says was removed. The only disclosure is price_known_steps=0 in the payload and per-slot price_known flags; no sensor or the card reads price_known_steps. Reach is narrow: a successful fetch with stale content, or a clock more than a day off (a failed fetch is handled honestly as UpdateFailed).

findings.title: The what-if solve shares learner containers with the loop by reference; a mid-solve write tears its answer
findings.claim: async_simulate's shallow replace(self._thermal_params) shares defrost_derate (the live DefrostDerate), internal_gains_profile and dhw_windows with the event loop while the what-if runs in the executor; an in-place write on them mid-solve changes the what-if's answer, whereas the live solve's deep copy is immune.
findings.mechanism: _solve_snapshot deep-copies state, params and config for the live solve; async_simulate uses dataclasses.replace, which copies scalars only. The only production in-place writer is _defrost.observe/observe_duty in _record_accuracy at the end of every cycle (draw pattern, gains profile and windows are reassigned, never mutated in place), so the realistic effect is one EWMA step landing mid-what-if; the what-if never actuates.
